info.bio:
Visage fue un conjunto musical representativo dentro del estilo "New Romantic" originado a fines de la década de 1970 con el motivo inicial de proveer música para ser reproducida en el club nocturno londinense Billy's, perteneciente a Steve Strange y Rusty Egan.

En sus inicios, el conjunto estaba compuesto por Steve Strange, Rusty Egan y Midge Ure. Ure e Egan iniciaron su trabajo musical con Strange después de la ruptura del grupo "Rich Kids".

scenes.name: New romantics y la escena del Blitz
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En el club Billy's y luego el Blitz, Rusty Egan pincha Bowie de Berlín, Iggy, Moroder, Kraftwerk, «Being Boiled», Telex y Yellow Magic Orchestra, y Steve Strange guarda la puerta: maquillaje, sombreros españoles y cortes geométricos, fantasía y escapismo tras ocho horas de trabajo. Visage, superbanda de punks fracasados (Ure, Currie, tres de Magazine), con la tristeza sobrenatural de «Fade to Grey»; Spandau Ballet, elitista y nietzscheano antes de volverse soul; Ultravox reformado con Midge Ure y la glacial «Vienna» (1981). Bowie lo corona con «Ashes to Ashes», con Strange vestido de Pierrot. Martin Rushent, con su sello Genetic, llegó a tenerlos a casi todos.

scenes.name: New wave y synth-pop en el Detroit negro
scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
scenes.author: Dan Sicko
scenes.desc: El new wave, que escondía una docena de variantes (punk, synth-pop, nuevos románticos, gótico, ska…), llegó al Medio Oeste vía Chicago y prendió entre el público negro de Detroit como en ningún otro sitio: los primeros discos electrónicos de la ciudad reconcilian a Human League, los B-52’s o Visage con el eurodisco, el funk de Clinton, Zapp y Ohio Players y el soul de Motown. Los preps adoraban los grupos de estética pulida; de Visage gustaba más que «Fade to Grey» su cara B instrumental, «Frequency 7». La Yellow Magic Orchestra fue un Kraftwerk más juguetón, y su «Technopolis» anticipa a Cybotron; ABC, Heaven 17 y Human League, desde la Sheffield siderúrgica, ofrecían una sofisticación fingida (Penthouse and Pavement, The Luxury Gap) que copiaron los clubes de instituto. Es la «doble refracción» de Jon Savage: los grupos europeos que idolatraban eran a su vez reflejo de la música negra americana.

scenes.name: Nuevos románticos
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: Movimiento londinense que rescata del glam el maquillaje y la pose, con un uso coyuntural de la tecnología: Ultravox (con John Foxx primero), Japan, Visage de Steve Strange, Duran Duran, Spandau Ballet, ABC, la pose kraftwerkiana de Gary Numan y, después, Culture Club.

podcast.body: Visage is highlighted as a prime example of New Romantic music, spearheaded by Steve Strange. Their sound contributed to the evolving electronic and synth-driven landscape of the scene. "A great example of New Romantic music is Vizage, headed up by Steve Strange."

podcast.title: New Romantic Movement Pioneers
podcast.body: Visage was a New Romantic band fronted by Steve Strange, who gained early exposure as an extra in David Bowie's influential 1980 music video for his "Scary Monsters" album. Bowie's video, with its fashionable and surreal clown character, was instrumental in jumpstarting the entire New Romantic movement of the early 1980s. "One of them was Steve Strange who would later head up his own new romantic band called Vizache."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin from Blitz Kids Movement
podcast.body: Visage was fronted by Steve Strange, who gained recognition as one of the Blitz kids featured in David Bowie's "Ashes to Ashes" video. The band's emergence reflects its roots in the Blitz kids' subculture and the broader New Romantic movement. "Steve Strange, one of the people in that video, would later front of band called Visage, which did okay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneers of 1980s Techno Pop
podcast.body: Visage is highlighted as a key act in the development of 1980s techno pop, a genre characterized by the pervasive use of synthesizers. They are grouped with other influential bands like Depeche Mode, Human League, and Yazoo. "And this brings us to the techno pop sounds of the 1980s, to Pesh Mode, Human League, Yazoo, Visage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneers of New Romanticism
podcast.body: Visage, like Spandau Ballet, was a New Romantic group whose origins lay in British clubs such as Billies and The Blitz Club, which fostered a scene for synth-based new music and a specific aesthetic. "One such offshoot was known as New Romantic, which had its roots in a couple of British clubs dedicated to new music. One was called Billies, and the other was the Blitz Club. This was the breeding site of groups like Spandovalet, Visage, and Culture Club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
